beat_player.text: You fought hard today, {player}. Your line held longer than most captains manage on the salt road. Bring more water next time and you will go further.
We took {troop_count} men off that road today. Nobody here needs to make more of it than it was. Mind your wells, friend.
You came at my flank like a captain who never learned to guard his wells, {player}. I took {troop_count} of yours. Think on that before the next march.
Ser {player}, you pushed me hard and I will say so at every fire on the road. The first war taught me to respect a line that does not break easily.

beat_by_player.text: Your timing was sharp, {player}. I lost {troop_count} men to a flank I should have seen coming. Well played.
You beat me fair, {player}. Mind your own wells now, and I will be watching your next march with respect.
I forgive slowly, {player}, but I will remember that ambush. Losing {troop_count} men hurts, and you knew exactly where it would hurt most.
Ser {player}, I have walked these roads since the first war and I still learn something from every loss. You taught me a new trick today, and I thank you for it.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and I broke {enemy_faction} at the ford with {troop_count} men. Good work, and good ground choice. I say it plainly.
We held together well, {player}. I have not fought beside a captain that calm since the old wars. Let us do it again soon.
Ser {player}, we held the line against {enemy_faction} and you never needed me to tell you where to stand. That is rare. Guard your wells and we will get along fine.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free, {player}, when a ransom would have been the easy choice. I will not forget that mercy at the next council.
{player} released me from captivity without asking for ransom. A rare kindness on the salt roads, and old hands will speak of it.
I thank you for the release, {player}. Mercy is worth more to me than any coin, and I will remember it.
{player} let me go without ransom. I accept the kindness, grudgingly, and I still count you among those who owe this realm a lesson.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The road is long but the company is worth it. Ask me anything and I will answer honestly.
You swore to {my_faction} and I believe you mean it, {player}. I will show you where the wells are kept, and where the traps are.
{player} has joined {my_faction}. We will see how you hold up in the next siege, though I am not one to judge a captain by his first week.
Joining {my_faction} does not buy you my trust, {player}. Prove yourself on the road and I may forgive you in time.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} is a fine holding, {player}. Our lord chose well, and I expect you to keep its wells full through the dry months.
So you have {fief}, {player}. I hope you remember that a town is only as strong as the wells beneath its walls.
{fief} goes to {player}. I have held better ground for less honor in the old wars, and I say that without rancor, mostly.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Come find me when the first harvest is in and we will talk over what it needs.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Your party looks well fed, and that is the first sign of a good captain on the salt road.
Good day, Ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}. Keep your distance and we shall get on well enough on this road.
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I remember your banners from Iggoudar, and I have not forgotten the truce. Keep your men back.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe roads, Ser {player}. Next time we meet, I will bring the good salt and you bring the stories.
Fare well, Ser {player}. The road is long, and so are the memories of this realm.
Off you go, Ser {player}. Mind the ford on your way, and do not test my patience on it again.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has come early to {town} this year. Old hands say that means a hard winter on the salt roads, so stock your wells now.
Heard that {village} has finally repaired its granary bridge. Good news for the road traders, and a relief to my old carts.
The north road out of {town} is quieter than it has been in years. Bring a spare horse anyway, because quiet roads have a way of changing.
I walked the first war roads near {village} as a young captain. The old stones still hold, if you know where to put your feet.

player_big_defeat.text: Hard luck, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men in one afternoon is a bitter thing, but many captains have rebuilt from less. Take heart.
I heard of the rout, {player}. Come sit at my fire when you are ready. I lost whole companies once and still walked home.
{player} lost most of their army and I will not pretend it is unfamiliar. Rebuild quietly, and the roads will forget.
I am sorry to hear of the rout, {player}. I will not gloat, though some on the road will. Learn from it and you may yet earn respect.
